lesson_changes.before: A continuous comparison function g is integrable on every finite interval. If f=g on the open interval(a,b), changing the two endpoint values does not change Lebesgue interval integrability or its integral. Transfer integrability with congr_uIoo and the integral with integral_congr_Ioo_of_le. The a=b case is included; no equality or continuity at a jump is required.
lesson_changes.after: Assume a<=b. A continuous comparison function g is integrable on every finite interval. If f=g on the open interval(a,b), changing the two endpoint values does not change Lebesgue interval integrability or its integral. Transfer integrability with congr_uIoo and the integral with integral_congr_Ioo_of_le. The a=b case is included; no equality or continuity at a jump is required.

lesson_changes.before: f=g\text{ on }(a,b),\quad g\in C^0\Longrightarrow\int_a^b f=\int_a^b g.
lesson_changes.after: a\le b,\quad f=g\text{ on }(a,b),\quad g\in C^0\Longrightarrow\int_a^b f=\int_a^b g.

lesson_changes.before: Induct on the number of grid intervals. The zero-interval integral and empty sum vanish. At the successor step, integrability of the prefix and last arc gives integrability of their union. The adjacent-interval identity adds the last integral, and the finite sum splits into its prefix and last index. This proves the exact sum for any nondecreasing finite grid without requiring positive lengths.
lesson_changes.after: Let the grid be nondecreasing; for every j assume g_j is continuous and f=g_j on(a_j,a_(j+1)). Induct on the number of grid intervals. The zero-interval integral and empty sum vanish. At the successor step, integrability of the prefix and last arc gives integrability of their union. The adjacent-interval identity adds the last integral, and the finite sum splits into its prefix and last index. This proves the exact sum for any nondecreasing finite grid without requiring positive lengths.

lesson_changes.before: Retain the exact twenty inherited definitions and six analytic assumptions. The simplex shows0<=a_n<=T, so the truncated terminal duration T-toNNReal(a_n) equals toNNReal(T-a_n). Thus the original tagged terminal weight is precisely exp(-h_n). The prefix density is the product of the n incoming rates and their arc survivals. Since the terminal exponential is nonnegative, ofReal transports multiplication exactly. Apply the product identity and substitute the proved integrated-hazard sum. Together with integrability and both incoming limits this closes the full frozen proposition. No normalization, all-count summation or signed-observable convergence is asserted.

No normalization, all-count summation or signed-observable convergence is asserted.
